problem.title: Fixed-window state trace (fictional assessment fixture)
problem.prompt: For an array of numbers, we want the sum of every contiguous group of k elements. Assume k is a positive integer; when n<k the output is empty. For [4,-1,2,7,0] with k=3, explain what state you retain and trace the first slide from indices 0..2 to 1..3. Explain why this reuse is useful, and what happens when n=k. Explanation only; do not implement or run code.

humanArtifacts.author: human
humanArtifacts.text: The state is the sum of exactly the k elements currently covered, with k a positive integer. Initially 4+(-1)+2=5. The next group is [-1,2,7], sum 8: subtract the outgoing 4 and add the incoming 7, so 5-4+7=8. Only those changed endpoints need updating, instead of summing all k elements for every overlapping contiguous group. When n=k there is one result, the initial total, and no slide. When n<k there is no complete group, so the specified output is empty. I have only reasoned about this; I ran no code.
